title: Signal-processing series aggregations
preamble:
# Signal-processing series aggregations

Three series aggregations that characterise the
*temporal structure* of event-driven boolean and rate signals —
`active_fraction`, `onset_rate`, and `integral` — together with the two
backing atoms they require (`SeriesBackendIntervalPulse`, `SeriesBackendNumericIntegral`; `onset_rate` reuses `SeriesBackendRingBuffer`).
Registered in [RDSC.7.1]. Prefix `LSIG`.

**Paired with:**
- [LSER] — the observation-triple framework these extend:
  aggregation vocabulary [LSER.16], per-type and agg×time-model matrices
  [LSER.17]–[LSER.18], warm-up and `t_first` [LSER.19], eviction [LSER.9.3].
- [LGRA.7] and [LSER.13.5] —
  the `gap-policy` series-line production.
- [LDET.3.6.1] — the correctly-rounded-op bar
  these backings hold to.
- [LNLS.3.5] — bounded-memory availability.

**What this is.** Point-process statistics — time-in-state and event rate
on boolean slots — and a time-weighted integral on rate slots. These
answer questions about *when and how long* events occur, which the
value-statistics vocabulary in [LSER.16] cannot express.

**What this is not.** Not spectral or amplitude DSP. DS carries no Fourier
or wavelet content, no RMS/energy, no filtering: those need a uniform
sample stream that DS's event-driven facts do not carry, and belong in an
at-the-ADC adapter (§[LSIG.9]). Nor the inter-onset *rhythm* statistics
(`mean_interval` / `interval_var` / `interval_stdev`).
